overview: The two major classes of flowering plants (angiosperms), distinguished by the number of seed leaves and several related structural features.
genZNote: Monocot: one seed leaf, parallel lines everywhere. Dicot: two seed leaves, branching networks everywhere.

aspects.label: Floral Parts
aspects.valueA: Flower parts typically in multiples of three.
aspects.valueB: Flower parts typically in multiples of four or five.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Parallel venation and fibrous roots always pair together in monocots — a fast way to identify them in a practical exam.
overlay.memoryTrick: Mono = one cotyledon, parallel veins. Di = two cotyledons, branching veins.
overlay.commonMisconception: Vascular bundle arrangement also differs (scattered in monocot stems, ringed in dicot stems) — a detail often forgotten beyond just leaves and roots.
